title: NOAA annual high tide flood day ranges contained 57% of observed counts at 85 US gauges in 2019-2025, less than the 68% expected, and their midpoints did not beat a 5-year mean
abstract: NOAA gives a likely range of minor high tide flood days for each tide gauge for the next May-April year. NOAA defines the range as the expected value plus or minus one standard deviation. We compared the as-issued outlooks for 2019-2025 with the observed counts from the NOAA CO-OPS API. The primary sample has 535 station-years at 85 gauges with no material threshold change. The observed count was inside the range in 56.8% of station-years (95% year-and-station bootstrap interval 45.5-67.8%), above it in 24.1% and below it in 19.1%. Coverage was 37% in the 2023 El Nino year and 43% in 2025. The ranges must be about 1.25 times wider to contain 68% (in-sample). The midpoint error (MAE 3.18 days) was smaller than that of last year's count (3.86 days; difference -0.68, interval -1.36 to -0.09). It was not smaller than the error of the 5-year mean (3.12), a 19-year linear trend (3.12) or a quadratic trend from 1950 (3.09). Region-by-year means explain 60% of the signed-error variance (permutation null 15%). Shared regional sea-level anomalies thus cause most misses. If you verify the pre-June-2023 Pacific Island outlooks with today's lowered thresholds, 76% of the counts are above the range. A recount with the old threshold gives 69% inside. This recount reproduces the counts that NOAA printed. Our 2019 coverage (60/23/17%) agrees with the value that NOAA reported. Limitations: only 7 verification years with correlated errors; the threshold history comes from indirect checks; the baselines are not the NOAA model.

display.caption: A: Share of 85 stable-threshold US gauges with observed minor flood days below, inside or above the NOAA likely range, by met year (May-April). The dashed line is the 68% expected for plus or minus 1 SD. B: Mean absolute error of the outlook midpoint and of three baselines that use only data before the met year. Grey bars show met-year mean ONI.

A: Observed flood days against the outlook midpoint (log scale, plus 1). B: Outlook MAE minus baseline MAE with 95% intervals from a bootstrap that resamples years and stations. Negative values mean that the outlook is better.
